title: 25 November
summary: Paratroopers from the bases north of Lisbon seized several air force units on 25 November 1975; the moderate wing of the Armed Forces Movement read the seizures as an attempted left-wing coup, while parts of the left described them as a reaction to the removal of radical officers already under way. The operation against them, commanded by Ramalho Eanes from a new operational command, was over within a day and cost few lives. Otelo Saraiva de Carvalho lost COPCON and the officers around him lost their commands, and the Communist Party, which had not moved, was left isolated. Historians still disagree about how far any coordinated left-wing plan existed; they do not disagree about the result, which was that the constitution then being written would be applied by a parliamentary republic and not by a revolutionary one. It is in the atlas as the endpoint where the several branches of 1975 converge.
